# Production evidence beyond the gate

Use this file for the product-specific acceptance and handoff that built-in checks cannot prove.
The skill and shared release gate remain authoritative; this reference adds no gate, waiver,
accepted-risk bypass or new automatic probe.

Name the release boundary, critical tasks, supported platforms/inputs, production-like environment,
protected contracts and evidence date. A planned checklist is not a result. Record passed, failed,
not verified or genuinely not applicable with the observed basis; an authorized risk decision stays
visible and cannot rewrite a blocking requirement as passed.

Choose manual coverage from actual promises and consequential changed seams: native assistive
technology, high-contrast settings, localization/RTL and input methods, virtual keyboard/safe areas,
intermediate content-driven reflow, actual deployed resource failures, and operational integration.
A personal device is not a support policy; emulation and physical-target observations are different
evidence. Name conditions and exact task/state rather than claiming all-platform certification.

For analytics, permissions, billing, delivery, support and rollback, distinguish synthetic stub
behavior from the real service. Existing owners verify their authorized integration; this reference
grants no production access, telemetry changes, rollout or policy commitments. Keep copy/asset approval
and data truth separate from design sign-off. A successful screenshot comparison proves no server
transaction, font license, support capacity or operational readiness.

Hand over confirmed outcomes, the still-unverified required work and responsible owner, stable
artifact/report locations and the exact fallback or rollback limits already supplied by the
project. Do not invent an expiry, mitigation, release window or service promise to close a gap.
